stories.title: In case of catastrophe on Earth the Moon could be humanity's salvation — Roscosmos CEO
stories.summary: MOSCOW, August 25. The Moon could become a backup location for humanity in the event of a major man-made or natural disaster on Earth, Roscosmos CEO Dmitry Bakanov has said. "Who knows what will happen on Earth? What man-made and natural disasters will occur? There must always be a backup option where humanity could 'relocate'. This will be impossible without space. The first stage is the Moon," he said in a comment to the Yunashev Live Telegram channel. Bakanov emphasized the utmost importance of developing all life support technologies on the Moon. "This is very important, because humans will need to be able to exist autonomously for some time before ecological systems are created," he explained. In May 2025, Roscosmos and the China National Space Administration signed a memorandum on the construction of a power plant for the International Lunar Research Station on the Moon. Roscosmos announced that the station would conduct fundamental space research and test technologies for long-term unmanned operation, with the potential for human presence on the Moon.

stories.title: Chennai Canvas: Madras Week Episode 4 | How cinema became part of Chennai
stories.summary: Cinema is woven into the fabric of Chennai’s cultural memory. From romance, longing and movie-inspired moments on the city’s beaches to the dramatic shift from celluloid reels to digital projection, Chennai’s relationship with the big screen has constantly evolved. At the heart of that journey are theatres that became landmarks in their own right, including Royapettah’s Pilot Theatre. Episode 4 of Chennai Canvas, for Madras Week, revisits these spaces, memories and technological changes to explore why, for generations of Chennai residents, the city and cinema have been inseparable.

In Episode 3 of Chennai Canvas: Madras Week, we explore three different threads that reveal the city’s enduring character.

From the unmistakable flavours of Chennai’s beachside food, shaped as much by the sea, salt air and atmosphere as by the food itself, to the story of how National Theatre brought cinema to the western suburbs, the episode travels through the city’s culinary and cinematic past.
Actors Nalini Nair, Nassar and Pasupathy also revisit favourite Chennai food memories, connecting personal nostalgia with the city’s changing food culture.
